newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower, Kia Group shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower, Kia Group shares fall.

text.p: Consolidation following a recent bull-run pushed Seoul stocks to close slightly lower for the second consecutive day on Thursday, brokers said.
Both domestic and foreign investors had recovered from the initial shock of North Korea's threat of war against the United States and South Korea. The threat was repeated on Thursday.
All six listed Kia Group shares showed no signs of recovering from market rumours of financial troubles, despite a strong denial by the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate.
The composite stock index lost 2.26 points to 770.95, off a day low of 763.18.
Brokers said North Korea's threat was no longer the main reason for the market's decline. Like domestic investors, foreigners were trying to realise a profit, they said.

"Foreign investors are now trying to take profits following the market's recent sharp gains because of the slow decline in interest rates and the yen's strength -- the most favourable factors affecting the local market," Lee Won-ki, managing director at Dongbang Peregrine Investment Trust Management Co.
Choi Dong-chul at Ssangyong Securities said: "Some foreign investors seemed shocked yesterday but their selling was eased today."
Brokers said investors now believed North Korea escalated tensions in the Korean peninsula whenever South Korea and the U.S. launched a military exercise.
North Korea issued a stern warning again against South Korea on Thursday, saying Seoul's recent war games were a "kind of declaration of war."
"The North Korean issue was just an excuse to sell stocks as everybody including foreigners had been monitoring the right time to take profits," said Choi Bum, trader at C.S. First Boston Securities.
But brokers said the market would consolidate further.

Asia Motors issued a statement to the Korea Stock Exchange, officially denying market rumours of financial troubles in the firm. But investors were unmoved by the denial and all six listed Kia Group shares declined.
Kia Motors and Asia Motors closed at their new yearly lows of 13,100 won and 4,030 won respectively. Asia was the most actively traded stock with 2.05 million shares changing hands.
"Regardless of the denial, the Kia issue will cause a polarisation in the market between representative industrials and the others," said Casey Choe at Union Bank of Switzerland.
Dong Ah Construction Industrial briefly went limit down to 17,800 won on the news the construction ministry had revoked its licence to build steel-framed bridges.
But it rebounded to close at 17,900 won, down 1,400.
The ministry found Dong Ah responsible for "mismanaging" construction of the steel-framed Songsu bridge which collapsed in October 1994, killing 32 people.
"This would make it impossible for Dong Ah to win a bridge construction order in the future," said a construction analyst at Hannuri-Salomon Securities.

Net profits of non-life insurers plunged to 56.16 billion won in the year, down from 132.74 billion profit a year earlier due to increased underwriting losses and operating expenses. But the insurance sub-index rose 4.70 points to 959.86.
Choi of Ssangyong said the market would consolidate to the 750 level without a recovery in the nation's major export items, including semiconductor and cars, in sight.
-- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
